title: Graceful Quota Delegation and Latency-Aware Tier Mapping for Mixed-Tier Traffic
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: We currently implement hard tier boundaries (free/paid/enterprise). When a higher tier exhausts quota or a region runs low capacity, requests fall back to lower-quality model variants or are rejected. This causes jarring behavior for customers (sudden latency spikes, hard 429s) and under-utilizes spare capacity in nearby pools.

Goal: Implement a quota delegation and latency-aware mapping layer that:
- Prioritizes enterprise > paid > free but allows controlled, auditable delegation of small-percentage traffic across tiers when safe.
- Uses latency and capacity signals to pick the best fallback variant (same model family quantized variant in region, smaller model, or cross-region route) while preserving SLOs for higher-paying customers.
- Enforces strict accounting so delegated usage consumes donor pool credits and is visible in billing and dashboards.

Success criteria / acceptance criteria:
- No customer-visible increase in median latency for enterprise traffic beyond +10ms at 95th percentile during delegation events.
- Delegation only occurs if donor pool has >15% spare capacity and will not drop below configured soft-reserve (default 80% utilization cap).
- Delegated requests are tagged and sum to a maximum of 5% of donor pool throughput by default; configurable per tenant.
- Billing records delegate usage and platform observability shows per-tenant delegated tokens.
- Feature is behind a flag and rolloutable per-region and per-tenant.

Design overview:
1) Admission & matches: incoming request annotated with tenant tier and SLA. Admission controller consults local capacity metric and target latency SLO. If local pool cannot satisfy latency SLO for the requested model variant, controller evaluates delegation candidates.

2) Candidate scoring: for each candidate (local alternative variant, cross-region same-variant, cheaper variant), compute a score = w1*estimated_latency + w2*cost_delta + w3*delegation_risk. Estimated_latency uses recent p50/p95 of the candidate route and KV cache hit rate. delegation_risk factors in donor pool spare capacity and tenant-specific soft-reserve.

3) Delegation rules & accounting: Only allow delegation when donor pool spare_capacity_pct >= donor_soft_reserve_threshold (default 15%). Each delegated call increments a "delegated_tokens" counter in tenant billing and updates the donor pool availability. Delegations expire/rollback if donor pool utilization rises above donor_soft_reserve.

4) Priority preemption: If an enterprise request arrives and donor pool must recover capacity, the system will preempt delegated work (best-effort requests flagged as "reclaimable") rather than dropping enterprise traffic. Preemption uses FIFO on time-since-delegation and priority-of-delegated-tenant.

5) Telemetry & observability: New metrics: delegated_tokens_total, delegated_requests_by_tier, delegation_latency_p95, delegation_reclaims, donor_pool_spare_pct. Dashboards and alerting rules to detect delegation runaway (>1% sustained across a region without human override).

Trade-offs and decisions considered:
- Full strict isolation vs. soft delegation: strict isolation is simplest for accounting but results in wasted capacity. We choose soft delegation with conservative caps to improve utilization while protecting SLOs.
- Cross-region delegation adds latency and multi-cloud cost complexity. We'll prefer same-region smaller variants first, then cross-region only if latency estimates remain within SLO.
- Delegation introduces billing complexity; we will surface delegated usage as a distinct line item and default to tenant-level opt-out via account settings.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Phase 1 (flags, no delegation): Expand admission controller to compute candidate scores and emit telemetry; tests only route to local fallbacks.
- Phase 2 (soft delegation off by default): Enable delegation path but capped and only for internal tenants; full logging and billing tagging.
- Phase 3 (gradual rollout): Allow selected customers to opt-in, increase caps, and iterate on preemption policy.

Pseudocode for admission decision:

"""
func select_route(request):
  candidates = enumerate_local_and_remote_variants(request.model)
  for c in candidates:
    c.estimated_latency = predict_latency(c, request)
    c.cost_delta = estimate_cost_delta(c, request)
    c.delegation_risk = compute_delegation_risk(c.donor_pool)
    c.score = w1*c.estimated_latency + w2*c.cost_delta + w3*c.delegation_risk
  sort candidates by score
  for c in candidates:
    if c.is_local && satisfies_slo(c):
      return c
    if c.is_delegation_candidate && donor_pool.has_spare_capacity and within_caps(c):
      allocate_delegation_token(c.donor_pool, request.tenant)
      return c
  return reject_with_429_or_queue(request)
"""

Edge cases:
- Burst storms: Temporarily halt delegation if delegation_reclaims spike > 10/minute and auto-alert ops.
- Stale metrics: Use short sliding windows (30s) for capacity signals with fallback to conservative defaults.

Open questions:
- Should delegated usage consume donor tenant quota for billing vs. be billed to the originating tenant at a premium? (PM prefers originating tenant billing; ops raised concerns about donor tenant visibility.)
- Fine-grained opt-in model: allow donor tenants to define a custom delegation percentage per model family.
updates: 2026-03-10: Kickoff meeting with PM, SRE, and Billing. Aligned on soft-reserve default of 80% and delegation cap 5% per donor pool.
2026-03-11: Spike implemented: added candidate scoring prototype and local latency predictor. Results: same-region smaller-variant median latency +8ms, cost delta -25%.
2026-03-12: Billing confirmed feasibility to tag delegated tokens; agreed on new billing line item 'delegated_tokens'.
2026-03-13: Implemented metrics emission for delegated_requests_by_tier and donor_pool_spare_pct; opened PR for admission controller changes (see PRs).
notes_for_qa: QA should simulate capacity shortfall in a region and verify delegation does not exceed configured caps.
Confirm delegated requests show the delegated_tokens billing tag and appear in tenant usage exports.
Verify preemption behavior: when donor_pool utilization rises, delegated requests should be reclaimed before higher-tier traffic is impacted.
